<text>
# Reform UK 2024 Manifesto Summary

## Immigration
The party proposes freezing non-essential immigration, leaving the European Convention on Human Rights, and implementing offshore processing for asylum seekers arriving from safe countries. Foreign criminals would face immediate deportation after serving sentences. A 20% National Insurance rate would apply to foreign workers (exempting healthcare workers and small businesses), with proceeds funding apprenticeships. Student visa rules would bar dependents, and a five-year residency requirement would apply before accessing benefits.

## Economic Policy
**Personal taxation:** Raise the income tax threshold to £20,000 (removing 7 million people from income tax), cut stamp duty (0% below £750k), abolish inheritance tax for estates under £2 million, and reduce fuel duty by 20p per litre while scrapping VAT on energy bills.

**Business:** Exempt businesses with profits under £100,000 from corporation tax, reduce the main rate to 15% by year three, raise the VAT threshold to £150,000, abolish business rates for high street SMEs, and introduce a 4% online delivery tax for large multinationals.

## Public Spending
Proposed savings include stopping Bank of England interest payments on QE reserves (£35 billion annually), requiring 5% efficiency savings across departments, halving foreign aid, and improving tax collection.

## NHS
Proposals include tax exemptions for frontline staff, 20% tax relief on private healthcare, removing student loan debt for medical staff serving 10 years in the NHS, and introducing patient vouchers for private treatment when NHS waiting time targets are missed. Weekend operating theatre use would be mandated.

## Energy
The party would abandon net zero targets, scrap renewable energy subsidies, fast-track North Sea oil and gas licensing, pursue shale gas extraction, and develop small modular nuclear reactors.

## Policing and Justice
Plans include recruiting 40,000 new officers over five years, implementing zero-tolerance policing, building 10,000 new detention places, introducing mandatory life sentences for repeat violent offenders, and reopening magistrates' courts.

## Education
Proposals include curriculum changes emphasising British history, banning gender identity teaching in schools, providing 20% tax relief on private school fees, scrapping student loan interest, and restricting undergraduate numbers.

## Benefits
The party would enforce a two-strike rule requiring benefit claimants to accept employment within four months or after two job offers, with face-to-face assessments for disability benefits.

## Defence
Spending would increase to 3% of GDP within six years, with a pay review for armed forces personnel, a dedicated veterans ministry, and recruitment of 30,000 full-time army personnel.

## Housing and Planning
Proposals include fast-tracking brownfield development, prioritising local residents for social housing, scrapping Section 24 tax rules for landlords, and abolishing the Renters Reform Bill.

## Transport and Infrastructure
HS2 would be cancelled, ULEZ zones and low traffic neighbourhoods banned, and petrol/diesel vehicle bans reversed. A 50% public ownership model is proposed for utilities.

## Agriculture and Fishing
The farming budget would increase to £3 billion with direct payments replacing climate-related subsidies. Foreign fishing vessels would require paid licences for UK waters, with supertrawlers banned.

## Constitutional Reform
Proposals include leaving the ECHR, replacing the House of Lords, reforming postal voting, and holding a referendum on proportional representation.

## Funding
The party claims £150 billion in annual savings plus £10 billion from additional economic growth, against £141 billion in annual costs.
